Subject: Eval gate exception: A/B acceptance & canary plan for Acme POC

Team —

Quick context: Acme's POC surfaced a subtle quality regression after we pushed promptset v14 -> v15 for the customer-specific intent routing. Their automated tests show a 0.9% drop in intent accuracy on a subset of high-value queries (sample attached), which tripped their internal SLOs. Acme's ok to continue the POC but asked for a clear acceptance/rollback plan.

As the cross-functional owners, we need a short decision: allow a scoped canary that relaxes the strict acceptance gates temporarily (exception) and rely on rapid rollback, or block the canary until we ship a narrower prompt patch. Proposed guardrails below — please comment by EOD so I can confirm with Acme:

- Canary scope: Acme account only, ramp from 5% -> 15% over 24h
- Acceptance criteria during canary: intent_accuracy delta >= -0.75% vs baseline AND hallucination_rate increase <= +1.0%
- Monitoring: realtime dashboard, automated alert if intent_accuracy drops >1.5% or error rate >0.5%
- Rollback SLA: 2 hours from alert (owner: Dev)
- Sampling/analysis cadence: daily ci-sampled reports and a full manual review after 48h

Attachments: eval_report_acme_20270412.pdf (summary), prompt_diffs_acme.csv (diffs).

Open questions for product/engineering: what is the minimum sample size we need to consider the A/B stable? Can we implement the 2-hour rollback runbook? Any objections on the numeric thresholds?

Thanks —
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova

Thanks for the write-up. Quick clarifying asks:

- Can we add a hard rollback trigger if customer-facing severity climbs (e.g., >0.3% of sessions flagged as "misrouted")?

I like the proposed ramp. For exec/CS visibility, I'll add a short summary to the Acme MAP doc and ping CS.

Short technical note from the eval/orch side:

- Sample size: with Acme's traffic profile, to detect a 0.75% delta at 95% confidence we need ~18k labeled samples per arm over 24h. If we can't get that, we'll rely on daily aggregated signals plus bootstrapped CIs.
- Stats gates: recommend a two-tier check: (1) quick check using rolling windows for obvious regressions (alerts) and (2) formal significance test at 24h and 48h.
- Ramp control: we can enforce account-level percentage targeting and a soft-cap of 15% for the canary. We'll also enable prefix caching to avoid inflated latency on new sessions.
- Rollback automation: I can provide a shell script to flip routing (Dev + infra approval) — rollback should be possible in <30m; operationally allow 2h SLA to troubleshoot.

I'll file the JIRA ticket for the automation piece (JIRA-SUP-3421) and attach the eval harness job config. If we proceed, I'll configure the alert thresholds in the dashboard.

-karthik

Thanks for the clear plan, Sofia. From Acme's side: we are comfortable proceeding with a scoped canary under the following conditions:

- Canary applies to Acme account only; 5% -> 15% ramp over 24 hours is fine.
- We require a documented rollback SLA of 2 hours and a single point of contact (Dev) who can execute it.
- We want a daily summary for the first three days and a checkpoint call 48 hours after start to review the manual analysis.
- If intent accuracy drops >1% or any high-severity misrouting incidents occur, we expect immediate rollback.

Please confirm timeline and provide the MAP link (contractual) and the contact who will be responsible for rollback.

All —

Recording decisions from the thread so we have a single source of truth:

1) Canary authorized: Acme-only; ramp 5% -> 15% over 24h (owner: Sofia to kick off with CS ops).
2) Acceptance criteria (both must hold):
   - intent_accuracy delta >= -0.75% vs baseline (daily rolling window)
   - hallucination_rate increase <= +1.0% absolute
   - customer-severity incidents ("misrouted" tags) <= 0.3% of sessions
   - latency p50 <= 120ms (slo)
3) Monitoring & rollback:
   - Alerts: intent_accuracy drop >1.5% OR misrouted >0.5% => immediate alert to on-call and Dev.
   - Rollback SLA: 2 hours to execute full rollback (Dev will run automated script; Karthik to own validation).
4) Sampling & analysis: Karthik to run significance tests at 24h and 48h; Marissa will do manual quality spot checks daily for first 3 days.
5) Communication: Daily summary delivered to Acme CS; 48h checkpoint call scheduled.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan_acme_v2.xlsx (updated with acceptance criteria), eval_report_acme_20270412.pdf. MAP link: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1AcmEvalGatePlan.

Owners:
- Canary kickoff & CS comms: Sofia
- Rollback execution: Dev Patel
- Alerts & eval harness: Karthik
- Manual QA: Marissa

If no objections by EOD today I will confirm the start time with Acme and deploy the canary window tomorrow morning.

Thanks,
